issue_context.title: TYP tighten `any` return type
issue_context.body:
Currently, `any` returns `Series | bool`.

However, for `DataFrame.any` the return type should be `Series`, and for `Series.any` the return type should be `bool`.

Marking as good first issue, but please only attempt this if you already have some experience with Python typing and `mypy`.
comments: Hi @MarcoGorelli I've always wanted to contribute to Pandas. Would I be able to be assigned this issue? Cheers
If you're familiar with mypy, sure, I'll assign you
@yadav-sachin I think you're OK to take this on if you want

review_comments:
The following is not necessary, feel free to ignore it.

It would be great to add overloads (depending on the type of level). The issue is that `None` is `Hashable` and `Level = Union[Hashable, int]`. I think the best we could do is to give a precise type in the default case of `None` and return a Union otherwise.

Something like this might work (did not test it)
```py
    @overload
    def any(
        self,
        *,
        axis: Axis = ...,
        bool_only: bool | None = ...,
        skipna: bool = ...,
        level: None = ...,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> Series:
        ...

    @overload
    def any(
        self,
        *,
        axis: Axis = ...,
        bool_only: bool | None = ...,
        skipna: bool = ...,
        level: None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> Series:
        ...

    @overload
    def any(
        self,
        *,
        axis: Axis = ...,
        bool_only: bool | None = ...,
        skipna: bool = ...,
        level: Level,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> DataFrame | Series:
        ...
```

You might want to test this with mypy (or pyright)
```py
reveal_type(pd.DataFrame().any())
reveal_type(pd.DataFrame().any(level=None))
reveal_type(pd.DataFrame().any(level="something"))
```

@twoertwein the issue is that then
```
df.any(0, None, None, None)
```
would result in
```
t.py:4: error: No overload variant of "any" of "DataFrame" matches argument types "int", "None", "None", "None"  [call-overload]
t.py:4: note: Possible overload variants:
t.py:4: note:     def any(self, axis: Union[str, int] = ..., bool_only: Optional[bool] = ..., skipna: bool = ..., *level: None, **kwargs: Any) -> Series
t.py:4: note:     def any(self, axis: Union[str, int] = ..., bool_only: Optional[bool] = ..., skipna: bool = ..., *level: Union[Hashable, int], **kwargs: Any) -> Union[DataFrame, Series]
t.py:4: note: Revealed type is "Any"
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

I think we're stuck between:
- waiting for arguments to become keyword-only
- adding 7 overload (!)
- assuming `any` will only be called with max 1 or 2 positional arguments

I think I'd have a preference for adding all overloads, and then removing most of them when the keyword-only deprecation takes places. Thoughts?

> * waiting for arguments to become keyword-only

In other PRs where we also have a deprecation warning, we write the overloads as if the keywords are keyword-only. Basically, you get two warnings: at runtime and at type checking time. This allows us to move a bit quicker with typing.

Ah, nice!

In that case, there's _a lot_ of redundant overloads that can be removed immediately

So yeah, happy to go with what you've suggested - @yadav-sachin want to make this change with the overloads?
I think this hasn't been formalized or written down. imho this is the first PR I'm aware of #45610
OK I'll ask on Wednesday, then we can come back to this

In yesterdays' meeting, it was agreed to type functions as if the deprecation was already taking place

So @yadav-sachin , do you want to follow @twoertwein 's suggestion in https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/46638#discussion_r842251078 ? (I think the first overload might be unnecessary)

> I think the first overload might be unnecessary

I think the first overload is needed when the user doesn't provide level. I didn't test it with mypy&pyright, but I think the second overload could be skipped (already included in the first overload).

> but I think the second overload could be skipped

🙌 yes, that looks like it (I also think it might not be valid syntax?)

> I also think it might not be valid syntax?

Are you referring to keyword-only arguments without default values? That is possible if they are listed after the `*`.

`# error: Signature of "any" incompatible with supertype "NDFrame"  [override]`

and same for pandas/core/series.py:4400: error: Signature of "any" incompatible with supertype "NDFrame"  [override]

Please check the output of mypy and add mypy ignore accordingly.

1. You can remove all of the self annotations (no need for `self: DataFrame` and `self: Series`)
2. We cannot yet have `*` for the implementation, only in the overload definitions
3. At the line of the first overload add the following ignore (all other lines do not need ignores):
```py
    # error: Signature of "any" incompatible with supertype "NDFrame"  [override]
    @overload  # type: ignore[override]
    def any(
```
4. run mypy locally (or let the CI run mypy)
